title: Workloads requesting a ResourceClaim stop being scheduled by Karpenter

detection.reason: the agent writes hasResourceClaims only when a workload HAS one, so a cluster with none cannot be told apart from an older agent that never wrote the key — the hint names the workloads that do carry claims

quote: Pods with `ResourceClaim` requests are explicitly ignored. Older revisions of Karpenter are not aware of the field and would ignore those requests. DRA is not currently supported by Karpenter.
remediation: Karpenter now explicitly ignores pods that request a ResourceClaim, and Dynamic Resource Allocation is not supported. The workloads named here get no capacity provisioned for them: they stay Pending unless a node they fit already exists. Older Karpenter releases ignored the field unknowingly and behaved the same way, so this makes an existing gap explicit rather than introducing one.
verifyCommand: kubectl get pods,deploy,statefulset,daemonset -A -o json | jq -r '.items[] | select(((.spec.template.spec // .spec).resourceClaims // []) != []) | "\(.kind)/\(.metadata.namespace)/\(.metadata.name)"'  # each workload printed requests a ResourceClaim and gets no Karpenter capacity
